name: system_monitor_tui
spec: Create a terminal-based system monitor in Python using only the standard library and curses. The application emulates htop-style monitoring with real-time updates, vim-inspired keybindings, and multiple views. All system data must be read directly from /proc and /sys filesystems without any external libraries like psutil.
features: Launches a full-screen curses TUI that updates every second by default
Displays CPU usage per core as individual progress bars with percentage
Displays a historical CPU usage graph using braille unicode characters showing the last 60 seconds
Displays total RAM usage, used, free, available, and cached memory in human-readable units
Displays swap usage with total, used, and free values
Displays system uptime in days, hours, minutes, and seconds format
Displays system load averages for 1, 5, and 15 minute intervals
Displays a process table with PID, user, CPU%, MEM%, state, and command name
Process table is scrollable with j/k vim keys and arrow keys
Process table can be sorted by CPU, memory, or PID by pressing c, m, or p respectively
Pressing / enters search mode filtering the process list by name in real time
Pressing Escape clears the current search filter
Pressing K on a selected process sends SIGKILL after a confirmation prompt
Pressing r on a selected process allows entering a new nice value to renice it
Displays a process tree view toggled with t showing parent-child relationships with ASCII tree lines
Displays network I/O per interface showing bytes sent and received per second
Displays disk usage for all mounted filesystems showing total, used, free, and percentage
Displays disk I/O read and write speeds in human-readable units updated per second
Displays battery status including percentage, charging state, and estimated time remaining if available
Displays active network connection counts by state parsed from /proc/net/tcp
Tab key cycles between views: Overview, Processes, Network, Disk
Color coding uses green for low usage, yellow for medium, and red for high across all meters
Pressing F5 forces an immediate refresh
Pressing q or F10 exits the application cleanly restoring the terminal state
Update interval is configurable via --interval flag defaulting to 1 second
All system data is read directly from /proc/stat, /proc/meminfo, /proc/net/dev, /proc/diskstats, /proc/uptime, /proc/loadavg, /sys/class/power_supply and related proc files without external libraries
